plan.estimand: R-squared in linear regression with 1 intercept + 3 predictors tested against zero
plan.hypothesis: H₀: R² = 0 (null model vs. full model with 3 predictors); H₁: R² ≠ 0
assumptions: Linear regression model with fixed predictors
Errors are normally distributed with constant variance
Test of global null (H₀: all regression coefficients = 0 except intercept)
Noncentral F-test using anticipated multiple correlation R = 0.30
scientific_notes: Power calculation for omnibus F-test in linear regression
Noncentrality parameter λ = (n × R²) / (1 - R²) applied to noncentral F distribution

answer.summary: For a fixed linear regression model with an intercept and 3 predictors, testing the omnibus null hypothesis H₀: R² = 0 against H₁: R² ≠ 0 using a noncentral F-test at α = 0.05 with n = 80 participants and anticipated multiple correlation ρ = 0.30, the statistical power is 0.624 (62.4%).
answer.method: Noncentral F-test for omnibus linear regression. The noncentrality parameter λ = (n × R²) / (1 − R²) where R² = ρ² = 0.09. The test statistic follows F(df₁ = 3, df₂ = 76) under H₀ and F(df₁ = 3, df₂ = 76, λ = 7.912) under H₁. Power is calculated as P(F > F_crit | H₁), where F_crit is the critical value from the central F distribution at α = 0.05.
assumptions: Linear regression model with fixed predictors and normal errors
Test of global null: all regression coefficients equal zero except intercept
Effect size (multiple correlation ρ = 0.30) is correctly anticipated
Errors are homoscedastic with constant variance
limitations: Power estimate assumes perfect specification of the effect size; power is sensitive to misspecification of ρ
Calculation assumes standard linear regression assumptions hold in practice
No inflation for model selection or post-hoc testing
Does not account for potential violations of normality in finite samples

# Power calculation for omnibus F-test in linear regression
# H0: R^2 = 0 vs H1: R^2 ≠ 0
# 
# Parameters:
n <- 80               # sample size (participants)
rho <- 0.30           # anticipated multiple correlation coefficient
k <- 3                # number of predictors (excluding intercept)
alpha <- 0.05         # significance level (two-tailed)

# Derived quantities:
R2 <- rho^2           # R-squared (effect size)
df_num <- k           # numerator df (number of predictors)
df_den <- n - k - 1   # denominator df (n - p - 1 where p = number of predictors)

# Noncentrality parameter for F distribution
# λ = (n * R²) / (1 - R²)
lambda <- (n * R2) / (1 - R2)

# Critical F-value from central F distribution at alpha = 0.05 (two-tailed)
F_crit <- qf(p = 1 - alpha, df1 = df_num, df2 = df_den, ncp = 0)

# Power = P(F > F_crit | H1 true) using noncentral F distribution
# This is the probability of rejecting H0 when the true R = 0.30
power <- 1 - pf(q = F_crit, df1 = df_num, df2 = df_den, ncp = lambda)

# Summary output
cat("================== Linear Regression Power Calculation ==================\n")
cat("Hypothesis: H0: R² = 0 vs H1: R² ≠ 0 (omnibus F-test)\n")
cat("Method: Noncentral F-test\n\n")
cat("Design Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Sample size (n):                 %d participants\n", n))
cat(sprintf("  Number of predictors (k):       %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("  Intercept:                       1 (included in model)\n"))
cat("  Total model parameters:          ", k + 1, "(intercept + 3 predictors)\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Effect Size & Test Specification:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Anticipated multiple correlation (ρ):  %.4f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("  R-squared (effect size):                %.4f\n", R2))
cat(sprintf("  Significance level (α):                 %.4f (two-tailed)\n", alpha))
cat("\n")
cat("Degrees of Freedom:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Numerator df:                    %d\n", df_num))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator df:                  %d\n", df_den))
cat("\n")
cat("Statistical Test:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Noncentrality parameter (λ):    %.6f\n", lambda))
cat(sprintf("  Critical F-value (F_crit):      %.6f\n", F_crit))
cat("\n")
cat("POWER RESULTS:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Power (1 - β):                   %.6f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("  Power (%% probability):          %.2f%%\n", power * 100))
cat("==========================================================================\n")

# Return structured result
result <- list(
  power = power,
  power_pct = power * 100,
  n = n,
  rho = rho,
  R2 = R2,
  k = k,
  df_num = df_num,
  df_den = df_den,
  lambda = lambda,
  F_crit = F_crit,
  alpha = alpha
)

# Emit result in required format
library(jsonlite)
results_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
  )
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(results_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
cat("\n")
